readme: One entry per person, shown in this order. Every entry has the same six fields: name and title as LinkedIn shows them, relationship in LinkedIn's words, when as the month and year in words, paragraphs as the recommendation word for word, and pull as one sentence of it quoted where there is room for one line. Nothing is reworded: a recommendation is the writer's, so the site quotes it or leaves it out. To add one, copy an entry and fill the six fields, then move the count the site states (ten, in RecommendationsTests and the About Steven document); the gate checks the shape.

recommendations.name: Meagan Colley
recommendations.title: Business Intelligence Analyst
recommendations.relationship: Meagan worked with Steven on the same team
paragraphs: In my time at Conway I was very privileged to have been mentored by Steven. His knowledge is very expansive as a full stack developer. As a result, I was able to learn a great amount from him. Steven taught me quite a few tricks and tips in regards to MySQL DB as well as Microsoft Azure and other front end tools. I know he has a wealth of knowledge in many other technical areas in addition to those mentioned. Our products ran on multiple languages and programs and he was the only tech person at the time, so he was the SME for virtually every product. Apart from his diverse technical knowledge, Steven was also professional and a joy to work with. He was very responsive to any issue or question a team member or client may have. He also was fantastic at problem solving; not only for quick fixes but also long term sustainability. I continue to be impressed by the improvements Steven has made to Conway's company products.
recommendations.pull: Our products ran on multiple languages and programs and he was the only tech person at the time, so he was the SME for virtually every product.
